title: Canonical factor through a scheme-theoretic image
statement:
Let $g:T\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, with scheme-theoretic image $\operatorname{SIm}(g)$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], defined by the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in $\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to g_*\mathcal O_T)$, and its closed immersion $g_{\mathrm{im}}:\operatorname{SIm}(g)\hookrightarrow Y$. Define the canonical factor map

$$
g^{\mathrm{im}}:T\longrightarrow\operatorname{SIm}(g)
$$

to be `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toImage g`. It satisfies $g_{\mathrm{im}}\circ g^{\mathrm{im}}=g$, namely `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toImage_imageι g`.

mathlib_match.how: exact: Hom.toImage (line 710) is the factor T ⟶ g.image for any morphism g, and Hom.toImage_imageι (line 715) says g.toImage ≫ g.imageι = g. Hom.image (line 662) is g.ker.subscheme and Hom.imageι (line 665) is g.ker.subschemeι; the latter is a closed immersion by the instance at Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean:94, applied to I = g.ker. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis is required. This is the image and inclusion in the current statement of def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image: its kernel ideal is exactly Hom.ker (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Basic.lean:692-694), defined using IdealSheafData.ofIdeals (:104-105), whose largest-subideal property is le_ofIdeals_iff (:125-126). The ordinary sheaf kernel is not substituted for that quasi-coherent subideal; no quasi-compactness is added.
